findings.reason: the mechanism is session-id-only and cannot see a run carried across a /clear, so the plan should either state that boundary or choose a key that survives it.
findings.text: §5 matches live pointers on `session` equalling the host owner's session id, and the file it cites for the FIFO's owner naming (`plugins/crew-host/bin/crew-host:2-8`) states the pair "survives /clear where the session id does not"; a run dispatched before a `/clear` keeps the old session id on its pointer (`live/*.json` carry no owner-pid field — checked on the newest live pointer, keys are backend, created_at, dispatch_options, due, hold, launch, launcher_host, local, named_route, node, phase, plan, project, queued_at, reason, repo, review_contract, run_id, section, session, urgency), so after a re-arm the host finds no live run and the pane stays empty in exactly the symptom this section exists to fix

findings.reason: the case cannot fail, so this one of §5's five done-when items gates nothing and lets §5 pass with its FIFO-removal coverage silently wrong.
findings.text: the fifth case ("The real host, signalled, removes its FIFO; and the real host whose owner exits removes its FIFO") measures behaviour that already exists at the base revision: `SessionHost.stop` calls `_remove_fifo` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:607`→`:615`) from both a signal (`run` installs SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers at :737) and owner exit, and §5 changes neither; the four declared negative controls cover only the first four cases, so no mutation of §5's own change can turn this case red

findings.reason: a done-when whose assertion target does not exist and is not named leaves the worker to guess, which is precisely where a plausible-but-wrong implementation passes its own test.
findings.text: §5 says the host "records in its `session-hosts` record ... that it is waiting for a dispatch" and the fourth case asserts "its `session-hosts` record says it is waiting for a dispatch", but `SessionHost.record()` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:368`) carries only `pid`, `owner`, `children`, `updated_at` (plus `stopped_at`/`stop_reason` on stop) and is written only on a child change; no field expresses "waiting for a dispatch" and none is named, so the assertion is unmeasurable until the worker invents both the key and its value

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `crew_host` (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2774`), `session_host.run` (:710), `SessionHost._remove_fifo` (:615, called by `stop` at :607), `_state_dir` (:117), `_TERMINAL_RUN_PHASES` (`reckon/crew/node.py:33` = complete/failed/stopped/interrupted), `LAUNCH_FAILED_PHASE` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:101`), `runs.py:2275` (`elif phase in {"failed", "launch-failed"}`), `resumption._pointer_session` (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:753`, reads `session_id`) and the four named tests in `tests/test_session_host_plugin.py` (:159, :178, :235, :258) all resolve; the extensionless-href convention does not arise here.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's fifth case (the real host removes its FIFO) has no declared negative control and passes unchanged on the base revision, so it cannot fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every log is "under the run directory", a durable path, and the new test file is a tracked path in the repository.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 names mechanisms and symbols only, with no plan labels, ticket numbers or changelog prose in the file paths or symbol names it introduces.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the start-up scan keys the owner to the Claude session id, which the plan's own cited script header says does not survive `/clear`, so a run left live across a `/clear` is still never followed.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable, the re-armed host following its own live runs, with its plumbing in one write-path set.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5 needs no new dependency edge: its write paths (`plugins/crew-host/bin/crew-host`, `session_host.py`, `crew_follow_commands.py`, `tests/test_session_host_plugin.py`) are disjoint from §2–§4's, and the open followup now invokes the whole plan rather than §2 alone.
